threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local DOCX comparison, editing, inspection and rendering engine, exposed through a Rust library/native CLI, a PyO3 extension/Python facade and CLI, wasm-bindgen byte APIs/Node CLI, and an optional Python MCP server over stdio. Inputs include untrusted DOCX ZIP/XML/media, legacy DOC and Markdown; outputs include changed DOCX, text/JSON reports, PDF and PNG. High-level operations admit packages before opening/DOM processing, with distinct default and comparison budgets. Rendering additionally discovers native host fonts and maintains a persistent font index. The native CLI explicitly supports GitHub self-update, including release lookup, checksum verification, delegated extraction and replacement of the running executable. Release tooling separately holds package-registry, GitHub and optional archive-signing authority. These are distinct interfaces and controls, not a single sandbox. Evidence: src/lib.rs:7-35, src/lib.rs:147-165, src/admission.rs:63-100, jubarte-python/pyproject.toml:47-55, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21, src/update.rs:186-257, .github/workflows/release.yml:230-269.
assets: Confidential input documents, extracted text/comments/authors, edit plans, resulting document bytes, reports and rendered pages. MCP text/inspection tools return document-derived content to the attached client; output paths also identify local resources. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-218, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:234-255.

Host process availability and memory/CPU, including the embedding Python interpreter and browser/WASM instance. Input admission is a resource gate rather than process isolation; supplied repository policy explicitly assigns residual CPU/memory isolation to hosts. Evidence: src/admission.rs:5-7, src/admission.rs:39-60, SECURITY.md:70-74.

Filesystem objects accessible through operator-authorized CLI paths, and document files beneath the MCP server's granted directory capability. Preserve existing outputs unless replacement is authorized, confine MCP document I/O, and expose partial-publication state. Evidence: src/publication.rs:146-206, src/publication.rs:448-469, src/publication.rs:558-570.

Native renderer font inputs and persistent font-index integrity. Fonts can originate from package embeddings, bundled catalogue faces, configured user font folders, system/Word fonts and Office cloud-font caches; the persistent index contains source paths/stamps used for subsequent file reads. Evidence: src/convert/mod.rs:806-807, src/convert/mod.rs:857-878, src/convert/font.rs:2258-2276, src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315, src/convert/font.rs:3154-3171.

Installed native executable integrity and release distribution authority. The updater currently trusts HTTPS release metadata/assets and SHA256SUMS.txt without a compiled release-signing key. The optional signing secret, CI GitHub token and local registry credentials are privileged workflow assets, independent of document processing. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48, src/update.rs:198-210, src/update.rs:245-257, .github/workflows/release.yml:261-307, .github/workflows/release.yml:356-369, scripts/release.sh:374-380.
trustBoundaries: Untrusted DOCX bytes -> admission -> OPC parts -> DOM/comparison/edit/rendering. InputLimits::default is 64 MiB compressed, 10,000 entries, 64 MiB per part, 256 MiB inflated total, XML depth 256. InputLimits::compare is 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB inflated total, with the same entry/depth limits. Both use defaults of 1,024 element attributes, 1,024 attribute-name bytes, 64 MiB raw/decoded attribute-value bytes and 128 MiB start-tag bytes. Overrides replace individual fields and reject unknown JSON keys. Evidence: src/admission.rs:63-164, src/xmllinq/parse.rs:48-57.

Different consumers have different admission budgets: inspect/edit Opened uses defaults, WmlDocument uses compare limits, and PDF/PNG layout calls document_comparer::admit_package, which uses compare limits. Raw file reads occur before the engine sees the bytes. These limits must not be modeled as an OS-level cap or a streaming limit on wrapper file acquisition. Evidence: src/inspect.rs:604-620, src/wml_document.rs:50-56, src/convert/mod.rs:769-778, src/document_comparer.rs:4926-4927, src/bin/jubarte.rs:2740-2742, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:141-145, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-55.

ZIP container metadata -> package identity and decompression. Admission checks preindex budgets, dual-header/extent/special-entry defects, safe part names, case-insensitive duplicate identities, encryption and compression methods before bounded reads; inflated bytes are counted rather than trusting declared sizes. Normal archive opening also runs zip_defects. Debug has a deliberate unchecked opener for triage. Evidence: src/admission.rs:439-553, src/opc/archive.rs:15-51.

Raw XML -> checked DOM construction versus explicitly permissive parsing. validate_xml_with_limits uses TagPolicy, enforces nesting/root structure and refuses DTD declarations and unsupported entities; public permissive parse_xdocument is not an admission boundary. OPC metadata has an independent 256-attribute cap. Evidence: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:918-958, src/opc/mod.rs:433-449, SECURITY.md:54-69.

Untrusted edit-plan data -> document mutation. The legacy edit transaction checks schema, optional exact source SHA-256, nonempty author and package admission before applying changes; a supplied source hash mismatching current bytes returns STALE_SOURCE. This optional digest binds bytes, not user identity or authorization. Evidence: src/edit.rs:2072-2099.

Native CLI -> ambient operator-authorized filesystem publication. publish_paths holds each chosen parent directory, stages bytes under that parent in .jubarte-<UUID>.partial/bytes, verifies length/content and installs by rename when overwrite is enabled or hard-link no-clobber otherwise. Unix staging directories use mode 0700. A group is atomic per file, not all-or-nothing, and errors record committed outputs and durability uncertainty. Evidence: src/publication.rs:83-143, src/publication.rs:203-220, src/publication.rs:420-505, src/publication.rs:535-570.

Python and Node CLI wrappers -> ambient filesystem authority, independently of native publication. Python Document.read reads the caller path; Python CLI _write uses Path.write_bytes, while Node CLI read/write uses fs.readFileSync/fs.writeFileSync and a separate exists/force check. Do not transfer native staged-publication guarantees to these wrappers. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/document.py:141-145, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:116-132, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79, jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-110.

MCP client -> explicitly granted document-directory capability. Startup resolves --root, defaulting to startup cwd, then holds _OutputRoot(cap_std::fs::Dir). Requested input names undergo containment diagnostics and are actually read through the held root; writes use capability-relative publication. docx_edit's derived outputs are <root>/<out_dir>/clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff and report.json, optionally redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png. docx_render derives page-NN.png and optional render.pdf. Overwrite defaults false. Tool annotations are metadata; access is shared by the attached stdio client rather than separate per-tool identities. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-108, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:153-217, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:220-255, jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381, jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1277, src/publication.rs:146-199.

Native renderer -> user font folder, outside any MCP document root. Effective folder precedence is nonempty JUBARTE_FONT_DIR, otherwise macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts; Linux nonempty $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts; Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/fonts. The host process and OS permissions own this capability. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652.

Native renderer -> persistent font index, separately from the font folder. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX empty/off disables it; another value names the index directly. Otherwise parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv yields macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/font-index.tsv or $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/font-index.tsv, and Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/font-index.tsv. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR therefore also relocates the default index into its parent. IndexEntry::load checks directory/file stamps before reading cached face paths; save merges and writes <index-path with extension tsv.<pid>.tmp> then renames it. This uses ambient fs access rather than OutputRoot. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:3095-3107, src/convert/font.rs:3154-3171, src/convert/font.rs:3182-3229.

Native renderer -> installed/Office font sources, independently of user-font and index resources. Family discovery includes fixed macOS font/Word directories and Windows ($WINDIR or $SystemRoot or C:\Windows)/Fonts plus $LOCALAPPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts. Office cloud candidates derive from $HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; family is constrained to one normal path component. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2225-2235, src/convert/font.rs:2281-2315, src/convert/font.rs:2855-2862.

Explicit native self-update -> GitHub metadata/assets -> installed executable. The fixed owner/repository is jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines; platform maps to macos/linux aarch64/x86_64 or windows-x86_64. Archive binary path is jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe]. The builder delegates checksum/extraction/swap to self_update 1.3.1, configures SHA256SUMS.txt and rejects extracted binaries that lstat as anything other than regular files. Interactive confirmation or --yes is required for installation; --check performs lookup only; explicit --version permits downgrade. RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean no signature is required now. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48, src/update.rs:91-108, src/update.rs:120-125, src/update.rs:144-160, src/update.rs:186-257, src/update.rs:307-320, Cargo.toml:137-148.

Tag/release maintainers -> release artifacts/signing/publication. CI builds five native targets, checks tag/version equality, and grants contents:write only to release publication. Optional ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY is injected only into Sign archives, decoded into $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN, used to sign dist/jubarte-*.tar.gz or *.zip and deleted by trap. Committed public keys require signing and verify every signed archive; checksums follow signing. GH_TOKEN receives secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN for gh release create in the current github.repository, publishing dist/*. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-49, .github/workflows/release.yml:58-74, .github/workflows/release.yml:230-307, .github/workflows/release.yml:317-322, .github/workflows/release.yml:356-369.

The script additionally executes an external app checkout's release-engine.sh; that implementation is absent from this repository and its authority cannot be established here. Evidence: scripts/release.sh:360-388, scripts/release.sh:914-919, scripts/release.sh:928-959, scripts/release.sh:1059-1069.

Developer-only benchmark worker -> ambient local paths. jubarte-rust-inproc is a long-lived stdin COMPARE worker, reading both requested paths and directly writing its output path. It is documented as a benchmark harness, not an authenticated hosted service. Evidence: jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:5-20, jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:29-68, jubarte-rust-inproc/src/main.rs:91-99.

Post-admission document metadata -> generated output/layout resources. HTML colspan expands into grid XML (src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-491,562-567); ordinary WML spans/skips expand layout vectors (src/convert/mod.rs:13600-13619,14204-14223,14340-14353); numbering levels/counters drive separate loops/labels (src/convert/mod.rs:5518-5533,5610-5629,6015-6019). Original package budgets do not by themselves bound these generated resources. These scenarios are reconciled with separate reported controls and deferred full renderer review.

Legacy DOC logical CP ranges -> character materialization. Public legacy read accepts FIB ccp_text and piece FC references (src/legacy_doc.rs:180-193,914-920,1084-1112), then produces StoryChar per logical character (src/legacy_doc.rs:1181-1225). Physical compound-file chain/offset checks do not impose a logical expansion budget. This boundary is reported separately from DOCX admission.

Embedded font bytes -> PDF subsetting. Package font parsing and glyf-backed face selection (src/convert/font_table.rs:212-242,src/convert/font.rs:1480-1501) precede raw table preservation, sfnt arithmetic and cmap enumeration (src/convert/pdf.rs:1208-1220,1286-1313,1434-1449,1531-1536). The caller must bound work/output even for a dependency-accepted font. Duplicate-directory arithmetic and cmap enumeration are independently reported.

Distinct local writer -> mutable wrapper publication names. Python and Node CLIs use preflight existence checks followed by truncating writes (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:101-133,jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-112) and predictable non-exclusive plan staging (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:403-413,jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:419-428). These conditional local boundaries differ from MCP/native held-handle publication and are reported separately.

Permitted PR contribution -> self-hosted runner account/private network. CI checks out PR-controlled source and executes local actions/Cargo on self-hosted runners (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-49); the configured mbx action documents a shared private cache network and persistent stores (.github/actions/mbx/action.yml:8-38). Docs, roundtrip and adoption expose sibling paths. Fork-run approval and actual runner isolation are external prerequisites; cache poisoning/root/release compromise are not established.

findings.title: Rendering an HTML altChunk with a large colspan exhausts process memory
findings.summary: Converting an attacker-supplied DOCX containing a small HTML altChunk can allocate tens of gigabytes before layout. The HTML importer accepts an unrestricted numeric `colspan` and emits one XML grid-column element per column; package admission only bounds original bytes, so a tiny input can terminate a native process or trap a WASM worker.

severity.rationale: High likelihood once an untrusted document is rendered: a simple, small HTML part deterministically requests billions of generated elements. Impact is process availability, not code execution or host compromise; remote/shared hosting is conditional.
severity.changeConditions: Isolated per-document workers with enforced CPU/memory limits constrain impact; exposing rendering in a shared long-lived service increases operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Independent static trace confirms public conversion reaches unrestricted span parsing and the allocation loop after admission. No live reproduction or memory measurement was run.

taxonomy.category: Unbounded allocation through HTML table expansion

codeEvidence.label: Public rendering expands admitted package content
codeEvidence.explanation: The DOCX supplier controls the HTML part returned by the relationship lookup; expansion completes before DOM construction and layout.

codeEvidence.label: The importer accepts unrestricted colspan values
codeEvidence.explanation: A valid positive decimal span becomes a usize without a maximum, so a short attribute can represent a billion columns.

codeEvidence.label: Cell spans determine generated grid size
codeEvidence.code:
let cols = table
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.iter().map(|c| c.span).sum::<usize>())
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1);
        let col_w = 9360 / cols;
codeEvidence.explanation: The maximum summed row span directly determines loop count, independently of input size or admission budgets.

codeEvidence.label: One generated element is allocated per column
codeEvidence.explanation: The String grows by a full XML element for each attacker-selected column, with no checked output-byte budget.

rootCause.summary: `with_layout()` admits the original package, then `altchunk::expand()` imports the relationship-backed HTML. `Builder::start()` parses `td`/`th` spans as unrestricted positive `usize` values. `Builder::end_table()` sums them and writes `cols` grid elements to a `String`. Neither the span nor generated bytes are bounded; admission cannot limit this post-admission amplification.

findings.remediation: Bound individual spans and aggregate columns before summation or iteration, use checked arithmetic, and impose a cumulative generated-WML byte/element budget shared across every HTML/MHT altChunk. Refuse excessive expansion with a typed input-limit error before allocation.

counterEvidence: ZIP and XML input admission exists but constrains original inputs, not generated WML.
SECURITY.md advises process CPU/memory limits; those contain termination to a worker but do not prevent this expansion.
No external fetch is needed: the HTML is an internal package part.
limitations: No application execution, crafted package, benchmark, or live deployment validation was performed.
validation.summary: Verified public PDF/PNG/report conversion shares `with_layout()`, which admits original input at `src/convert/mod.rs:773` then expands HTML/MHT parts at lines 789-798. `admission.rs:535-558` limits original inflated bytes and treats `.html` as non-XML. A single cell with `colspan="1000000000"` causes one billion 20-byte grid elements before DOM construction, about 20 GB of generated text alone. No cap or checked generation budget intervenes.

dataflow.summary: Attacker DOCX -> admitted original package -> relationship-backed HTML -> `html_to_wml()` -> positive usize span -> summed columns -> repeated String writes -> memory/CPU exhaustion.

impact.why: Resource exhaustion can terminate or trap the rendering process and interrupt colocated work.

likelihood.why: A short numeric attribute directly controls a large allocation loop after admission.

reachability.summary: A document supplier needs a consumer to render their file. Rust public conversion APIs and Python/WASM wrappers reach this shared layout path; MCP `docx_render` is an additional conditional host. The attacker does not need filesystem/environment configuration or release authority.
reachability.attacker: Supplier of an untrusted DOCX or its HTML altChunk
preconditions: Consumer renders the supplied document; remote service exposure is not assumed.

findings.summary: When a user selects an output directory writable by a distinct lower-trust local actor, that actor can replace an output name with a symlink after the wrapper's no-force existence check. Python and Node then follow the mutable name in a truncating write, allowing replacement of another file writable by the victim process without `--force`.

severity.rationale: Source confirms an unauthorized write redirection, but exploitation requires a separate local actor with write access to the chosen output directory and a target writable by the victim. This constrained, deployment-dependent path is lower likelihood than a document-only attack.
severity.changeConditions: Private output directories remove the distinct-writer prerequisite. Shared directories across different accounts or privilege levels increase risk.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently verified both precheck/direct-write implementations and rendering callers, plus native/MCP countercontrols. No race reproduction was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Python checks existence before work
codeEvidence.explanation: The no-force decision is made before the pathname is opened.

codeEvidence.label: Python later performs a truncating pathname write
codeEvidence.explanation: The final write does not carry overwrite authorization or enforce exclusive/no-follow creation.

codeEvidence.label: PDF generation separates preflight from publication
codeEvidence.explanation: Rendering creates a substantial interval after no-force preflight and before the write at line 757.

codeEvidence.label: Python publishes render bytes through the mutable name
codeEvidence.explanation: PDF and PNG bytes flow through the same direct-write helper.

codeEvidence.label: Node checks existence separately
codeEvidence.explanation: existsSync does not bind the later open or make creation exclusive.

codeEvidence.label: Node follows the destination at write time
codeEvidence.explanation: Default writeFileSync follows links and truncates rather than enforcing no-clobber at commit.

codeEvidence.label: Node checks then renders then writes
codeEvidence.explanation: A distinct writer can replace the destination pathname during conversion.

rootCause.summary: Python `_ensure_writable()` and Node `ensureWritable()` observe existence before output work. Their `_write()`/`write()` helpers subsequently open the pathname for truncating output without exclusive creation, no-follow policy, or overwrite authorization bound to the final operation. Rendering places computation between the check and write. PDF, PNG, document/text and report publication in Python and PDF, document/text/JSON and Markdown comparison publication in Node inherit that gap.

findings.remediation: Use staged verified publication with held parent-directory authority for both wrappers. Carry overwrite authorization through commit and atomically refuse any existing destination when force is false; do not rely on a preliminary exists check.

counterEvidence: Document supply alone cannot control a private output directory.
Stable existing outputs are refused when force is absent; input/side-file identity checks address ordinary aliasing.
MCP uses OutputRoot and native publication uses held handles plus atomic no-clobber hard links; these routes do not inherit this helper.
limitations: A shared mutable output parent and distinct attacker/victim authority are required.
No application execution or race timing measurement was performed.
validation.summary: Verified the Python PDF precheck at line 741 precedes `doc.render()` and `_write(output, rendered.pdf)` at 757. Node renderTo performs the same sequence at 150-152. A separate writer can install a symlink after a missing-file check; final Path.write_bytes/fs.writeFileSync follows it and truncates its referent under victim permissions. Sibling writers use the same helpers. No final no-force check is atomic with opening.

dataflow.summary: User-authorized output name -> non-atomic existence check -> conversion -> attacker pathname substitution -> truncating symlink-following write.

impact.why: An unrelated victim-writable file can be truncated/replaced with generated output.

likelihood.why: Requires a shared mutable output directory and distinct local authority boundary.

reachability.summary: The affected interfaces are ambient Python and Node CLIs, not the root-confined MCP publisher. The attacker needs separate permission to modify selected parent entries, while lacking direct access to the ultimate target.
preconditions: Victim selects a directory another actor can modify.
Target is writable by victim process and not directly writable by attacker.

attackPath.summary: A victim renders or converts to an absent output in a shared writable directory. A distinct actor replaces that output name with a symlink to a victim-writable existing file between preflight and publication.

remediationTests: With a deterministic fake publication backend, insert a destination after preflight and assert no-force commit refuses without touching its referent.
Use filesystem integration tests for symlink replacement and preserve native/MCP no-clobber behavior.

extensions.groupingRationale: Python and Node observations share the same broken precheck-only no-clobber policy and staged-publication remediation; all language-specific callers and sinks are retained.
extensions.originalWorkerSeverity: medium; parent calibrated low for the constrained distinct-local-writer prerequisite.

findings.title: Predictable plan staging files can redirect Python and Node writes through symlinks
findings.summary: Python and Node plan recording use a staging filename derived from the plan basename and process ID, then open it with ordinary truncating write APIs. A distinct actor able to create entries in that directory can precreate the staging name as a symlink, causing generated plan JSON to overwrite a file writable by the victim process before the final rename.

severity.rationale: Impact is unauthorized truncation under victim permissions, but it requires a distinct local writer of the plan directory plus knowledge/prediction of target basename and PID. Private directories remove the prerequisite.
severity.changeConditions: Shared directories across accounts or privilege levels increase impact. Exclusive private staging prevents the path.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified recording/preview callers and both predictable staging writes. No runtime exploit or filesystem mutation was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Python uses a predictable staging name and non-exclusive write
codeEvidence.explanation: An attacker-precreated partial symlink is followed by write_bytes before the rename.

codeEvidence.label: Node uses the same predictable plan staging pattern
codeEvidence.explanation: PID plus target basename determines a partial file opened without exclusive creation or no-follow semantics.

rootCause.summary: After successful plan generation/preview, Python `_record()` resolves the target and constructs `.<target>.<pid>.partial`; Node `recordPlan()` constructs the same pattern. Neither reserves the name exclusively. `Path.write_bytes()` and `fs.writeFileSync()` follow an existing staging symlink and truncate its referent. The subsequent replace/rename cannot undo that prior write, so staging does not preserve the intended publication boundary.

findings.remediation: Use an exclusively created private staging directory/file held by handle, verify staged bytes, and atomically publish to the authorized plan target. Refuse preexisting staging objects and preserve intended final-plan symlink semantics without following a staging symlink.

counterEvidence: The selected plan path may intentionally be a symlink; this finding concerns an independently attacker-controlled staging name.
Dry-run does not publish.
Private plan directories prevent a distinct writer from precreating the partial.
The native publisher uses an exclusive UUID staging directory and is a separate implementation.
limitations: No application code or vulnerability-triggering input was executed.
Attacker must learn/predict the plan basename and victim PID and write directory entries.
validation.summary: Verified each non-dry-run plan-recording branch writes the predictable partial before replacing the final target, without create-new/no-follow flags or a private staging directory. A precreated staging symlink is therefore followed at the write itself. Plan validation checks document edits, not filesystem authority of the staging name.

dataflow.summary: Authorized plan recording -> predictable partial path -> non-exclusive symlink-following write -> unrelated referent overwritten -> final rename/error cleanup.

impact.why: Unrelated victim-writable files can be truncated and replaced with plan JSON.

likelihood.why: Shared-directory and predictable-name prerequisites constrain reachability.

reachability.summary: Python and Node edit/add plan-recording branches reach these sinks after a valid preview. Document-only control is insufficient; a distinct lower-trust actor must be able to create staging-directory entries.
preconditions: Attacker can precreate the derived partial name and target is writable by victim.

attackPath.summary: Before a victim records operation flags into a plan in a shared directory, precreate its basename/PID partial path as a symlink to a victim-writable file. Plan JSON is written through that link before rename.

remediationTests: Precreate the derived staging name as a symlink in a filesystem integration test and assert its referent remains unchanged.
Verify safe plan recording, dry run and failure cleanup through a deterministic publication backend.

findings.title: Permitted fork pull requests execute code on the shared self-hosted runner pool
findings.summary: Pull-request workflows check out contributor-controlled source on self-hosted runners and execute checkout-local actions, Cargo build scripts/tests and repository scripts. The configured pool is documented as sharing persistent stores and a private tokenless cache service. Once a fork run is permitted, contributor code receives runner-account filesystem and private-network authority.

severity.rationale: Executing untrusted contribution code in a shared persistent runner environment can have high infrastructure impact, but likelihood depends on fork-workflow approval and actual runner isolation. Exact cache poisoning, credential theft, release compromise and host-root access are unproven.
severity.changeConditions: A disposable isolated runner without trusted persistent state/private-service access removes the stated boundary. Reusable privileged runners or shared release credentials would increase severity.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified event triggers, self-hosted placement, PR checkout and executable steps, plus source-documented shared resources. Live GitHub approval, runner lifecycle, mounts and network filters were not supplied.

codeEvidence.label: PR checkout runs on self-hosted infrastructure
codeEvidence.code:
lint:
    name: fmt + clippy
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@89b12181fb390509a0842a86cc55eeb8eb928c1d # stable branch, pinned 2026-10-01

          components: rustfmt, clippy

codeEvidence.label: Shared private cache is exposed to those runners
codeEvidence.code:
# The self-hosted runners share one mbx cache server on their private Docker
# network (`mbx-cache`), so a crate one runner compiled is a cache hit on the
# others. The server takes no token: mbx sends none over plain HTTP, and only
# the runners can reach it. mbx publishes only from pushes to a protected
# branch; pull requests read. GitHub-hosted runners cannot reach the server,
# so jobs that also run there keep Swatinem/rust-cache on those legs.
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: jdx/mr-boxington-action@47ce49b32025d93a7a2f4570815afaa2b7092240 # v1.7.2
      with:
        backend: remote
        version: "1.24.1"
        remote-url: http://mbx-cache:7543
        namespace: jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines
codeEvidence.explanation: Repository configuration documents a shared private network/cache with no token and configures its endpoint.

codeEvidence.label: Runner checkout and stores are reused
codeEvidence.code:
# Every job on a runner builds in the same checkout, so mbx always counts
    # that checkout's managed target as the most recently used and never
    # collects it: on 2026-10-17 three of them reached 69-220 GiB in a few
    # hours and filled the disk the four runners share. Each job now starts
    # from an empty target, restored from the store and the cache server,
    # and each runner's store keeps to a fixed share of the disk.
    - name: bound mbx's disk use
      shell: bash
      run: |
        echo "MBX_GC_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE=20GiB" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
        mbx clean --under "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        MBX_GC_MAX_TOTAL_SIZE=20GiB mbx gc
codeEvidence.explanation: The documented execution environment shares persistent stores/disk; it is not configured as an isolated per-PR job here.

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@89b12181fb390509a0842a86cc55eeb8eb928c1d # stable branch, pinned 2026-10-01

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@c18668ad3cf93ea998bef934396af7bb5c839dc7 # v10.2.0

codeEvidence.label: Adoption executes PR tests on self-hosted runner

  claims:
    name: adoption claims (tests/adoption.rs)
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:

rootCause.summary: CI admits `pull_request` events without a same-repository/trusted-ref gate for self-hosted jobs. The checkout runs before local composite actions and Cargo commands, so a contributor can modify an action, build script, test or invoked script. Read-only token permissions and disabled credential persistence do not isolate that code from the runner account. The mbx action configures a private cache endpoint and documents reused checkouts/stores/shared disk; no per-PR isolation boundary is configured in these workflows. Docs, roundtrip and adoption expose the same pool through independent PR paths.

findings.remediation: Run untrusted PR jobs on GitHub-hosted or disposable isolated workers without trusted persistent stores/private services. Gate access to the shared self-hosted pool using trusted workflow logic outside PR control. Enforce cache read-only access at the service boundary when PRs need it.

counterEvidence: GitHub may require approval before fork workflows run; that prerequisite is explicit.
contents:read and persist-credentials:false reduce GitHub token exposure but do not sandbox executable code.
External runner/container isolation and cache-server authorization implementations are absent.
The cache comment says PR clients read only; no server write bypass is established.
Fork-rejecting Jules workflows and GitHub-hosted security jobs use different boundaries and are not implicated.
limitations: Live approval policy, runner lifecycle/mounts/network ACLs and cache protocol were not queried.
No untrusted code, workflow run or cache request was executed.
validation.summary: Verified `pull_request` trigger, `runs-on: self-hosted`, ordinary checkout, checkout-local action and Cargo execution in CI. Verified sibling docs/roundtrip/adoption placement and commands. The mbx composite action explicitly configures http://mbx-cache:7543 and documents a shared private network, no token, reused checkout and persistent stores. Thus permitted PR code runs with that environment's account/network authority under the documented pool configuration.

dataflow.summary: Fork PR checkout -> self-hosted runner -> local composite/Cargo/repository script -> runner account filesystem and configured private cache network.

impact.why: Untrusted code obtains runner-account filesystem/private-network authority beyond an isolated contribution test environment.

likelihood.why: Fork approval and actual runner isolation are external prerequisites.

reachability.summary: A contributor needs a permitted pull-request workflow run. No privileged GitHub token is needed for code to inherit runner-account resources; the claimed impact assumes the source-documented shared pool rather than an independently isolated disposable deployment.
reachability.attacker: External contributor controlling a permitted fork PR
preconditions: Runner deployment exposes the documented shared persistent state/private services.

attackPath.summary: Submit a PR that changes an executed local action, Cargo build script/test or repository script; after the run is permitted, a self-hosted job executes it in the documented shared runner environment.

remediationTests: Statically check that fork/untrusted PR execution cannot select the shared self-hosted pool.
Verify isolated workers have no trusted persistent volumes/private cache write credentials and that server-side cache permissions match caller trust.
